Seeing the woman rearranging things in her purse before closing it, something caught Martina’s eye. At first she thought it was a piece of jewelry she had shifted to the top. Then it became clear as the woman’s hand went around it, what she saw was as small silver pistol, obviously, with pearl grips. Instantly going to her thigh, Martina came up with the Savage 32 semi-automatic. Leveling it at the woman, she was fully prepared to shoot if that hand came from the purse, the silver pistol in it. But it didn’t, fortunately for the woman, who closed the purse and sat it back at her feet. Returning the gun to her thigh, Martina felt she couldn’t blame the woman for having the pistol, being she carried so much money

on her. But it did seem a bit out of character for a woman of her age to possess a gun in the first place. Let alone be walking around with at least twenty grand cash in her purse. But then, this was Vegas. Anything could happen here, and did. Twenty minutes later, the woman was out of chips again. This time, however, she simply gathered up the purse and walked away, allowing some man behind her to happily take her place at Gloria’s table. Finding nothing else to capture her attention, Marti made her way to the stairs, to go below again. Reaching the floor, she passed through a bank of slot machines before catching sight of Slade Brannagan, coming her way. “Martina,” he greeted cheerfully. “Why are you on the floor today?” “Actually, I was hoping to catch sight of Harry Dunbar. He should be here by now,” she said, as a worried look came over her face. “Listen, Martina.” Slade smiled. “I grew up with Harry. And if there’s anything I’ve learned over the years, it’s that he, perhaps, is the most unpredictable man in the world. Hell, he may not show up until next week. The best you, or anyone, can do is be patient.

Rest assured though, if he said he was coming, he’ll be here … eventually.” “Even though I have no reason to doubt what you said is true, I still can’t help but feel anxious,” Martina said. “I just hope nothing happened to him en route.” “Well, if it’ll make you feel any better, Martina … Tomorrow, I’ll call around … see if I can locate him. That is, if he doesn’t show up by then. We have a mutual friend in Phoenix. Maybe he’s gone there for a short visit.” “Thanks.” They started to walk. “You bet.” “You know, I’m almost ashamed to ask this, but … was Harry ever married? I mean, he never mentioned a wife in the time I knew him.” “He was, in fact, married to a beautiful woman for twenty or so years. Unfortunately, she died of cancer two years ago,” Brannagan said. “It was sad. I didn’t think Harry would recover from that. But he eventually did.” “I’m sorry, I didn’t know.” “Don’t be, Martina! That’s just a part of life. It happens to the best of us. And the

sooner you learn to live with it, the better off you, and all concerned, will be.” “You sound as though you’re talking from personal experience, Slade?” Martina searched his face. “I am, Martina.” Feeling her eyes on him, he looked away to nothing in particular. “The mother of my children is in a home for the mentally insane. She doesn’t know me or her children any longer. But I’ll never divorce her. She still means that much to me.” She wanted to say she was sorry again, but dared not. “Does Gloria know about this?” “She does. I told her not to say anything. She’s a great gal, Martina,” Slade said, with sincerity in his tone. “When she told me about her third husband … it made me want to go kill the bastard myself.” “You sound like you know who did … kill him.” “I do. Harry told me all about it, but said I should keep a lid on it.” “Good!” Martina said. “Let’s keep it that way … And yes, Gloria is a great gal. She’s had a hard life, Slade … It’s about time she found a man that will treat her right, for a

change.” “Well, if you’re referring to me, Martina … Rest assured …” Just then, Martina saw the redhead that had been at Gloria’s table coming back into the casino. She wouldn’t have been all that alarmed had it not been for the determined way she was walking. That, along with the fact that she had her purse tucked under her left arm, and her right hand buried inside it. Martina took two quick leaps to the side, separating herself from Slade, then reached for the gun under her dress. Had she not felt a need to do that, she may have gotten the Savage out in time. The woman had already passed by Gloria’s table, and was presently a mere twenty feet from Martina. Now the silver pistol was leveled squarely at Martina’s head. “Hold it right there, Miss Spalding!” the woman said, and tossed aside the sunglasses, exposing eyes ablaze with hatred. Comprehending that, Martina froze, and came slowly back up to her own height. Her mind was awhirl with possibilities as to what to do next. “What is it you want with me?”

The first thought that came to mind was that this was Jamie’s step-mother. But that was silly. Why would she care, the way he talked … “You killed my boy!” the woman screamed. “And poor Lenny! Why did you have to kill my brother? Now you’ll die … bitch!” She extended her gun-arm. Now it was only a few feet from her. The last thing Martina saw, before taking a dive for the floor, was Slade charging in from the side. Then the gun fired … and she heard nothing more.

CHAPTER ELEVEN “Martina,” Gloria said from her knees, on the floor beside her. Then she felt the slaps to her hand and began to come around. “What the hell happened?” She felt like she had been hit by a bus, and put a hand to her head. Feeling nothing wet, she tried to get up. “I sort of pushed you into a slot machine,” Slade said. “I’m sorry. Are you okay?” He helped her to her feet. Still a bit uneasy, Slade continued to support her. Looking around, she asked, “Where is she? The redhead …? Was that Raym’s mother … for God’s sake?” “Security took her out right away …” Gloria said. “I’m sorry, Martina. With that wig and those dark glasses, I didn’t recognize her. And she didn’t talk at all … Not once …”

“I … I heard a gunshot… Did she shoot somebody?” “No. Thanks to Slade, she never got the chance,” Gloria said. “You shot her?” Martina said, turning to see him behind her. “I didn’t know you carried a gun.” “I could say the same about you … Miss Spalding.” Brannagan chuckled from frustration. “I guess between the two of us, we did okay.” “What did I do,” Martina said, trying to figure how she’d been of help. “That little maneuver you pulled. It took her attention away from me long enough to pull my gun, unnoticed,” Slade said. “If it wasn’t for that, we may both have been riddled with bullets.” “Is she dead?” Martina asked, hoping against hope that another hadn’t died for what she’d done … by killing Raym. “No,” Slade said. “She’ll live. I shot her in the foot. It’s an old Chicago trick. The shock of being shot in a foot will stop an attacker faster than a slug through the heart. It’s very painful!”

“I’ll have to remember that,” Martina said, cringing at the thought. “What’s her name? I don’t think I ever heard …” “Virginia …” Gloria said. “And to think, I always liked her.” “Let us through!” Brannagan said to the people gathered around. “It’s over, folks! Go back to your games!” He then marched Martina toward the archway entrance to the hotel. In the room, then, over a cup of tea spiked heavily with brandy, the gravity of what had happened came over Martina. “Oh, my God!” Tears filled her eyes. “Will it ever end? Now that they know where we are, who will come next?” That’s when she came to the realization it was no longer Gloria they were after: Virginia seemed to have no interest in Gloria at all. If she had been, she could have shot her at any time while at her table. There was no doubt in Martina’s mind now Virginia Koffee was here for the sole purpose of locating and killing her. She was their only target now. And it appeared, regardless of the deal cut with Harry Dunbar and the St. Louis Police Department, they weren’t going to give up on

her, either. Or had the mother of Raym, as well as being the sister to Lenny, simply gone rogue, driven by remorse? And where was Harry, anyway? If he were here, maybe some sense could be made of all this. “I’ve got to go,” Martina finally said, looking into the faces of Gloria and Slade at the table where they sat. She didn’t give them time to react, and went on talking without pause, and without the luxury of having prepared what to say. “I mean, it’s clear to me now, this is not over, not by a long shot. Harry as much as said so when I talked to him on the phone. Even he suspects others will come. Me being here only serves to endanger your lives as well. Especially you, Gloria. If anything should happen to you …” With that, Brannagan stood from the table. He seemed greatly concerned. “I can’t tell you what to do, Martina. But I can offer some advice, if you’ll let me?” “I would appreciate that,” Martina said, letting her eyes slide up to meet his. Brannagan selected his words carefully.
